newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard to drop 5 routes, add New York.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard to drop 5 routes, add New York.

text.p: Vanguard Airlines Inc said Monday it planned to eliminate service on five routes but would begin service to New York City.

Vanguard said it would stop serving Des Moines, Iowa, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, and the Orlando and Tampa-St. Petersburg markets in Florida, after September 2. By halting service to Las Vegas and Los Angeles, Vanguard said it would end all late-night flights.
The company said it would begin offering daily non-stop flights between Kansas City, Missouri, and John F. Kennedy (JFK) Airport in New York, effective September 3.
"By concentrating our fleet in fewer markets, we can offer increased frequency and greater reliability," Robert Spane, chairman, chief executive and president of Vanguard Airlines, said.

"Our strategy is to focus on larger business markets, especially where Southwest Airlines does not fly, and to provide service above that of a typical low-cost airline. These changes allowed us to add JFK to our route system as well as increase frequency to popular business destinations we already serve."

In addition, the company said it signed a letter of intent to lease an eighth aircraft from Interlease Aviation Corp for delivery September 1. It said it was considering leasing two more aircraft by the end of the year.
